name: 99.co
description: 99.co (99 Group) is a Singapore-headquartered real estate technology company and one of the largest property marketplaces in Southeast Asia. Founded in 2014 by Darius Cheung, Yan Phun and Conor McLaughlin, it operates consumer property portals across Singapore and Indonesia, including 99.co and SRX.com.sg in Singapore and 99.co/id and Rumah123.com in Indonesia. The platform lets buyers, renters and agents search HDB resale flats, executive condos, condominiums, landed homes and new-launch projects for sale and rent, with map-based search, transaction data, agent directories, mortgage tools and nearby-amenity insights (MRT, schools, commute times). 99 Group is backed by investors including Sequoia Capital, 500 Global, Golden Gate Ventures, Quest Ventures and East Ventures. This profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; 99.co exposes consumer web products but publishes no first-party public developer API or portal at this time.

name: Alodokter
description: Alodokter is Indonesia's leading digital health and telemedicine platform, founded in 2014 and operated by PT Alodokter Teknologi Solusi. It connects tens of millions of monthly active users with tens of thousands of licensed doctors through chat-based consultations (Tanya Dokter), online and in-person doctor appointment booking, a large library of medically reviewed health articles and a symptom and disease encyclopedia, health protection and insurance products, and a health commerce surface for medicines and health products. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and enriched from the provider's own public web surface; Alodokter does not publish a public developer API portal or OpenAPI at this time, so this profile focuses on company identity, legal and support surfaces, and domain security posture.

name: Aruna
description: Aruna is Indonesia's largest integrated fisheries commerce platform, on a mission to make the sea a better livelihood for all by building a fair and sustainable fisheries ecosystem. Aruna connects more than 40,000 small-scale fishermen to domestic and global markets using technology, a network of processing partners, and 177+ distribution hubs (Aruna Hubs) across the Indonesian archipelago, trading 23+ seafood commodity types into 31+ countries. The company pairs commerce with sustainability work, including fisherman education, fish-population tracking, and coastal-community empowerment. Aruna is a portfolio company of Prosus Ventures and was added to the API Evangelist network as a company lead; it publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API surface at this time.

name: Astro Sea
description: Astro (PT Astro Technologies Indonesia), operating at astronauts.id, is an Indonesian quick-commerce platform that delivers groceries and everyday essentials in as little as 15 minutes. Its consumer mobile apps (iOS and Android) offer more than 3,000 curated products spanning fresh produce, frozen goods, groceries, beauty, household items, and electronics, with 24/7 service across the Greater Jakarta (JADETABEK) region. Astro is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners and was surfaced through that portfolio into the API Evangelist network. Astro is a business-to-consumer application company; it publishes a consumer app, a corporate site, and an RFC 9116 security contact, but does not currently expose a public developer API, OpenAPI definition, SDKs, or developer portal.

name: Bandung Institute of Technology
description: Institut Teknologi Bandung (ITB) is a public research university in Bandung, Indonesia, ranked #256 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. ITB operates a number of public-facing web systems including an institutional digital library (Ganesha Digital Library / GDL), an academic portal, and a campus-wide single sign-on service. As of this review ITB does not publish a dedicated developer portal or documented public API program; its machine-readable surfaces are limited to a CAS-based SSO endpoint and an institutional repository whose historical OAI-PMH/RSS endpoints no longer resolve after a platform migration. The entries below reflect only what could be verified live and publicly.

name: Bank Jago
description: PT Bank Jago Tbk is a technology-based digital bank in Indonesia, listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX: ARTO) and backed by investors including Ribbit Capital and GoTo. Rather than a branch network, Bank Jago is delivered through the life-centric Jago mobile application and is deeply embedded into partner ecosystems — Gojek/GoPay for payments, and Bibit/Stockbit for investing — via API-based integrations. Its Open API payment surface is exposed through Indonesia's national SNAP (Standar Nasional Open API Pembayaran) programme, administered through the ASPI developer directory, rather than a self-hosted public developer portal. Bank Jago is regulated by the Indonesian Financial Services Authority (OJK) and Bank Indonesia. This API Evangelist profile is compiled from public sources as a fintech company lead; the bank publishes no self-hosted OpenAPI, SDK, or developer documentation at this time.

name: Brik
description: Brik ("[Re]Constructing Construction") is an Indonesian construction-materials company, backed by Accel, that operates concrete batching plants and supplies ready-mix concrete for building and infrastructure projects across the Greater Jakarta region, including Bekasi, Bogor, Karawang, and Bandung. Its product line spans standard ready-mix batches and higher-performance "Super Concrete" variants used for mass-concrete pours. At the time of enrichment Brik publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or webhook surface; this record is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company profile.

name: Bukalapak
description: Bukalapak is one of Indonesia's largest online marketplaces and all-commerce platforms, connecting millions of individual sellers, small warungs (kiosks), and buyers across the archipelago, alongside virtual products, financial services, and online-to-offline retail. Originally added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub (backed by 500 Global), this profile has been enriched from Bukalapak's real public developer surface: a public REST API at api.bukalapak.com secured with OAuth2 via accounts.bukalapak.com, a first-party JavaScript SDK (bukalapak.js), and a large public GitHub organization. No OpenAPI/Swagger specification is currently published by the provider, so the captured artifacts (authentication, packages, domain security) are sourced from first-party repositories and live domain probes rather than derived from a spec.

name: Dagangan
description: Dagangan is an Indonesian tech-enabled wholesale e-commerce platform serving small and medium retailers (SMEs) in tier 3-4 cities and rural areas. Through a hub-and-spoke network of 50+ micro-warehouses across remote regions, it connects large suppliers to traditional local retailers, giving them affordable mobile access to daily necessities and groceries while reducing delivery costs and supply-chain friction. The company operates a consumer/retailer Android shopping application (Dagangan Mall), is backed by 500 Global, and is recognized as a Rural Digitalization Partner of Indonesia's Ministry of Villages, Disadvantaged Regions, and Transmigration. As of this profile, Dagangan publishes no public developer API or OpenAPI specification.

name: Eatsii
description: Eatsii is a Jakarta, Indonesia based foodtech startup operating a cloud kitchen platform. It runs a cloud kitchen concept that offers takeaway and delivery alongside dine-in service, and markets cloud kitchen space to F&B operators under a franchise partnership model, positioning itself as helping food and beverage companies run a more efficient kitchen in the food delivery era. The company describes itself as combining a heartfelt touch with data and business strategy, and lists 11-50 employees in Food and Beverage Services. It was surfaced through the 500 Global (500 Durians) portfolio. Eatsii publishes no developer program, public API, or technical documentation, and as of July 2026 its eatsii.com domain does not serve a live website.

name: Edukita
description: Edukita (PT Edukita Budaya Cinta Belajar) is an Indonesian education company founded during the COVID-19 pandemic by Peter Gumulia and Sean Widjaja on the belief that high-quality education should be accessible to all. It teaches skills that matter through playful but powerful learning, delivering programs online, through six physical learning centers across Greater Jakarta (Bintaro, Bogor, BSD, Depok, Gading Serpong), and blended (Rumah Belajar Edukita). Programs span English with native speakers, early childhood development, Japanese mathematics, and professional upskilling for young students, families, adult learners, and corporate training. Edukita is a portfolio company of 500 Global. It exposes no public developer API surface at this time; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture.

name: eFishery
description: eFishery is an Indonesian aquaculture technology ("fishtech") company founded in 2013 in Bandung by Gibran Huzaifah and Chrisna Aditya. Its platform combined an IoT smart auto-feeder (eFeeder) that dispenses feed to fish and shrimp ponds and streams pond telemetry to a smartphone app, with an integrated services layer: eFisheryKu / eFarm farm-management software, eFund (including the Kabayan "pay later" financing product) linking smallholder farmers to lenders, and eFresh / eMart marketplaces connecting farmers to feed suppliers and downstream buyers. The company raised a $90M Series C (2022) and a $200M Series D (2023) at a unicorn valuation, backed by investors including 500 Global, Aqua-Spark, SoftBank Vision Fund 2, Temasek, and Northstar. In late 2024 an audit alleged large-scale financial-statement fraud dating to 2018; both founders resigned and the company underwent multiple rounds of layoffs and restructuring through 2025. This record was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; eFishery exposes no public developer API or developer portal, and its primary efishery.com domain currently resolves to a parked/forwarding host.

name: Fairbanc
description: Fairbanc (PT Fairbanc Technologies Indonesia) is a Jakarta-based digital finance platform that uses AI/ML-powered credit scoring to deliver embedded, revolving supply-chain financing and buy-now-pay-later "terms of payment" to micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) across Indonesia. Working with trusted financial institutions and distributor/supply-chain ecosystems, Fairbanc provides merchants with an instant digital facility limit and short-term working-capital liquidity at the point of purchase — with no formal loan application, smartphone, or app required — plus data intelligence and consulting that help distributors reduce bad-debt risk and grow transaction value. The company reports its terms-of-payment product drove roughly 35% distributor sales growth. This is a company profile in the API Evangelist network; Fairbanc publishes a consumer-facing marketing and onboarding site but no public developer/API program at this time.

name: Finku
description: Finku is an AI-based personal finance management (PFM) mobile app from Indonesia, recognized as the number-one Indonesia PFM app and a Google Play "Best of 2025" selection with more than one million users. It helps people track expenses, set budgets, and build better money habits through manual entry, receipt and bank e-statement scanning, and FinGPT, a chat-based AI financial assistant. The app connects multiple banks and e-wallets, generates real-time interactive dashboards and reports, and runs a freemium model with a Premium tier. Finku is registered with Indonesian regulators OJK, Kominfo, AFTECH, and AFPI, and secures user data with 256-bit AES encryption. Finku is a consumer application and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile originated as a VC-portfolio lead for the API Evangelist network.

name: Five Jack
description: Five Jack (PT. Five Jack) is the Indonesian company behind itemku, one of Southeast Asia's largest digital-goods marketplaces for gamers. Founded in 2014 as a game price-comparison and classifieds platform, itemku grew into a full marketplace where buyers and sellers trade in-game items, currency, account top-ups, game keys, and vouchers across 200+ game categories including Roblox, Genshin Impact, Mobile Legends, Dota 2, Steam, and Growtopia. The company reached one million orders in 2018, launched its Android app and gaming blog in 2020, and became part of Bukalapak (IDX: BUKA) in May 2021. Five Jack was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. It operates a consumer-facing marketplace and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal.

name: Flip
description: Flip (PT Fliptech Lentera Inspirasi Pertiwi) is an Indonesian financial technology company offering low-cost interbank money transfers, bill payments, and cross-border remittance to consumers, and a "Flip for Business" (bigflip) suite of payment APIs to companies. The Flip for Business API lets businesses disburse money to any Indonesian bank or e-wallet (Money Transfer / Disbursement API), accept online payments via bank transfer, virtual accounts, e-wallets, cards, and retail outlets (Accept Payment API), and send international transfers (International Transfer API). The API is HTTP Basic authenticated with a secret key, supports IP whitelisting, idempotency keys, and signed callbacks/webhooks, and ships a sandbox environment plus WooCommerce and Magento 2 payment plugins. Flip is backed by Insight Partners, Lightspeed Venture Partners, and Y Combinator.

name: Gadjah Mada University
description: Gadjah Mada University (Universitas Gadjah Mada, UGM) is a public research university in Yogyakarta, Indonesia, and is ranked #239 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. Its public, machine-consumable developer footprint is limited: the institutional repository (EPrints "repository civitas UGM") exposes a working OAI-PMH 2.0 metadata endpoint for harvesting scholarly output, and the university operates a centralized CAS single sign-on service. Most academic and administrative systems (SIMASTER, admissions) sit behind authentication, and there is no public, documented developer portal.

name: GoTo
description: GoTo (PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk, IDX: GOTO) is the largest technology group in Indonesia, formed in May 2021 through the merger of the on-demand and ride-hailing pioneer Gojek and the e-commerce marketplace Tokopedia. GoTo operates a super-app ecosystem spanning on-demand services (ride-hailing, food and grocery delivery, logistics), e-commerce, and financial technology through GoTo Financial (including GoPay, one of Indonesia's leading digital wallets). The group serves Indonesia's population of more than 270 million, connecting tens of millions of consumers with millions of merchants and driver-partners, and is estimated to contribute roughly 2 percent of Indonesia's GDP. GoTo is backed by a roster of blue-chip investors including SoftBank Vision Fund, Alibaba, Google, Tencent, Temasek, and Sequoia Capital India. This company profile was surfaced as a SoftBank Vision Fund portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline. Note that GoTo Group's developer surfaces are published per product (Gojek/GoBiz, Tokopedia, GoTo Financial/Midtrans) rather than at a single group-level developer portal; this record profiles the parent holding company.

name: GoTo Group (Gojek + Tokopedia)
description: GoTo Group (PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk) is Indonesia's largest digital ecosystem, formed by the 2021 merger of ride-hailing / on-demand superapp Gojek and e-commerce marketplace Tokopedia. It operates three business pillars: On-Demand Services (Gojek — ride hailing GoRide / GoCar, food delivery GoFood, parcel delivery GoSend, logistics GoBox, courier GoSend), E-Commerce (Tokopedia marketplace and Mitra Tokopedia), and Financial Technology (GoTo Financial — GoPay, GoPayLater, GoInvestasi). In 2024 GoTo divested Tokopedia's e-commerce operations to TikTok Shop / ByteDance, retaining a 25% stake in the combined Tokopedia–TikTok Shop entity; the developer.tokopedia.com portal now redirects to TikTok Shop's partner platform. GoTo continues to operate Gojek and GoTo Financial directly. There is no single GoTo group-wide developer portal — partner integrations happen at the product level (Gojek partner programs, GoPay PSP integrations, TikTok Shop Open Platform for the former Tokopedia surface).

name: GoWork
description: GoWork is Indonesia's largest premium coworking and flexible office space provider, operating more than 25 locations across Jakarta, Tangerang, Surabaya, Bali, and Medan. Formed from the 2018 merger of GoWork and Rework, the company offers private offices, dedicated desks, coworking memberships, virtual offices, meeting and event spaces, plus podcast and live-streaming studios. It also bundles business services such as company incorporation, tax and accounting, visa and work-permit processing, and legal support. Members discover, book, and manage workspace through the GoWork mobile apps and web booking platform. GoWork is backed by 500 Global and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile.

name: Hangry
description: Hangry is an Indonesian multi-brand virtual restaurant and cloud-kitchen company founded in 2019 and backed by 500 Global. It designs, operates, and delivers a portfolio of consumer food brands - including Moon Chicken, San Gyu, Ayam Koplo, Dari Pada, Wai Thai, Pizza Gang, and Accha - engineered to be tasty, consistent, and affordable for the mass market and sold primarily through third-party food-delivery channels. Hangry operates as a direct-to-consumer food and beverage business rather than an API or developer platform provider; it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface. This profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment tracking.

name: HD
description: HD is an AI-native healthcare marketplace and patient-navigation platform for emerging Southeast Asia, headquartered in Bangkok, Thailand. Its consumer surface, HDmall, is a health, dental, aesthetics, and surgery marketplace that lets patients compare transparent pricing and book online across 30,000+ services from 3,000+ clinics and hospitals in Thailand (hdmall.co.th) and Indonesia (hdmall.id). AI-powered navigation turns patient symptoms into personalized, safety-checked care recommendations, and HDcare adds human-led, AI-assisted concierge support for complex surgical cases. The platform has navigated over 500,000 patients. HD is a consumer-facing healthtech operator with no public developer API or portal; the strongest machine-readable surface it publishes today is an llms.txt guiding LLMs to its canonical content. HD is a portfolio company of Partech, added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment tracking.

name: HijUp
description: HijUp is an Indonesia-based modest-fashion e-commerce marketplace selling Muslim women's clothing online — abayas, blouses, dresses, tunics, printed scarves, hijabs, mukena, khimar, and related accessories — aggregating a large catalog of local Indonesian modest-wear brands (over a hundred labels listed under its brands directory) into a single storefront with international shipping. The company operates a consumer-facing shopping site (product catalog, categories, cart, checkout, and customer accounts) rather than a public developer platform; it publishes no API, SDK, or developer portal at this time. HijUp is backed by 500 Global and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile. Public contact is customer@hijup.com and +6221-78-24-001.

name: IDRX
description: IDRX is a stablecoin pegged 1:1 to the Indonesian Rupiah (IDR), issued by a regulated Indonesian entity and available across multiple EVM chains and Solana. Its REST API lets business (organization) accounts onboard KYC-verified users, register bank accounts, and process mint (fiat IDR -> IDRX / USDT on-chain), redeem (IDRX -> fiat IDR to a bank account), and bridge (cross-chain) transactions, plus query swap rates, fees, supported bank methods, and transaction history. Requests are authenticated with an API key and an HMAC-SHA256 request signature, and settlement is confirmed via single-delivery webhooks or transaction-history polling. IDRX is a portfolio company of a16z (crypto).

name: Kata.ai
description: Kata.ai is an Indonesian enterprise conversational-AI company that builds AI agents and chatbots for customer experience, marketing, sales, and HR across financial services, retail, healthcare, automotive, and government. Its developer-facing Kata Platform lets teams create bot projects that bundle a Bot, CMS, and a Natural Language Understanding (NLU) model, then deploy them and connect messaging channels such as LINE, Telegram, WhatsApp, Facebook Messenger, Slack, and Qiscus. Kata.ai exposes a public REST API for managing projects, bots, deployments, environments, channels, teams, and NLUs, an NL Prediction API for entity extraction from a trained model, the kata command line tool, and the Aksara design system. Backed by 500 Global.

name: Komerce
description: Komerce is an Indonesian end-to-end e-commerce enabler serving more than 50,000 online sellers and SMEs with an integrated suite covering fulfilment, logistics, marketplace operations, CRM, advertising and payments — Komship, Kompack, Komplace, Komchat, Komcards, Komtim, Komads and Komclass. Its developer surface is published under the RajaOngkir brand and exposes four APIs: Shipping Cost (Cek Ongkir) for domestic and international rate lookup and airway-bill tracking across 17 Indonesian couriers, Shipping Delivery (Komship) for creating orders, requesting pickup, printing labels and tracking shipments, Payment Service for Virtual Account and QRIS transactions with signed callbacks, and QRISLY for turning a static QRIS into dynamic per-transaction QRIS codes. All four authenticate with a per-product header API key issued from the Collaborator dashboard, and the delivery, payment and QRIS products run a full isolated sandbox.

name: mucho
description: Mucho (Mucho Indonesia) was an Indonesian social-commerce startup founded in 2018 and headquartered in South Jakarta, positioned as Indonesia's first social online shopping application and often described as an aspiring "Pinduoduo for Indonesia." Its mobile app let users buy together with friends to unlock group-buying discounts, cutting distribution layers by working directly with brand owners and pairing frictionless payment with logistics support. The company raised early / seed funding with participation from Qiming Venture Partners. Mucho has since shut down; its app is no longer distributed and the mucho.asia domain now resolves to a parked placeholder page with no product, API, or developer surface. This profile is retained as a defunct-company record surfaced through the Qiming portfolio graph.

name: Mycotech
description: MYCL (Mycotech Lab) is an Indonesian biomaterials company, founded in 2015 and based in Bandung, that cultivates mushroom mycelium on agricultural waste to produce sustainable, carbon-sequestering alternatives to animal leather, plastics, and construction materials. Its flagship product is Mylea, a mycelium-based leather-like material, alongside Biobo binder board, MYCL Composite for architecture and interior design, and Mylea Sea, a seaweed-based biopolymer. A certified B Corp and Good Design Award winner backed by 500 Global and the Unreasonable Group, MYCL sells physical materials and finished goods rather than software; it publishes no public API, developer portal, or developer documentation.

name: Pazpo
description: Pazpo was an Indonesian property-technology (proptech) marketplace that billed itself as the country's first property search engine ("Mesin Pencari Properti Pertama di Indonesia"), letting users buy, sell, and rent homes, shophouses (ruko), apartments, warehouses, offices, and land across Jakarta, Tangerang, and the wider Indonesian market via web and a companion mobile app. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global (500 Startups) and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead for the enrichment pipeline. The enrichment pass found the company defunct: the pazpo.id domain no longer resolves (DNS lookup fails), and by 2024 the lapsed domain had been taken over by an unrelated Indonesian online-gambling ("togel") site. No live website, developer portal, API, SDK, or documentation surface exists to harvest; historical detail here is reconstructed from Internet Archive captures (2015-2017).

name: Pintarnya
description: Pintarnya is an Indonesian technology startup, launched in May 2022, that operates an employment and financial-services super-app for the country's blue-collar and entry-level workforce (education levels from elementary school through bachelor's degree, "SD-S1"). The platform aggregates tens of thousands of daily-updated job listings across 300+ Indonesian cities and pairs job search with Cari Cuan side-income tasks, Siap Kerja skill-building video courses, a CV builder, and an employer/recruiter posting product used by tens of thousands of companies. Pintarnya reports more than 10 million registered job seekers and is registered with Indonesia's Ministry of Labor (KEMNAKER). It is a consumer web and mobile product; no public developer API, OpenAPI description, or developer portal is published as of this profile.

name: Pintu
description: Pintu (PT Pintu Kemana Saja) is an Indonesian cryptocurrency exchange and investment app founded in April 2020 and headquartered in Jakarta. Licensed as a Physical Crypto Asset Trader (PFAK) under Bappebti and now supervised by the OJK, Pintu serves more than four million retail users with spot trading, crypto futures, staking/Earn, and a self-custody Web3 wallet connecting to DeFi and NFT dApps. Beyond the consumer app, Pintu operates Pintu Pro, an institutional and partner trading platform whose HMAC-signed WebSocket + HTTP API (docs.pintu.pro) lets market makers and partners place and cancel orders and stream execution reports and trades against production and sandbox environments. Pintu has raised over 150M USD across a Lightspeed-led 35M Series A+ (2021) and a 113M Series B (2022) with Intudo, Pantera Capital, and Northstar.

name: Samastha Synergy Pte. Ltd.
description: Samastha Synergy Pte. Ltd. operates Djoin (djoin.id), positioning itself as a "digital partner for sustainable scale" that helps financial institutions and organizations in Indonesia grow through an adaptive product ecosystem. Djoin's named products are Coopmax (a platform aimed at cooperatives / koperasi), Kocek, and ProofyLink. The company runs a private backend API at api.djoin.id, which sits behind Cloudflare and returns 403 to unauthenticated requests; as of this profile there is no public developer portal, OpenAPI/Swagger definition, documentation, or SDK surface published. Samastha Synergy was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; this profile captures what is publicly verifiable from the djoin.id site and DNS/TLS probes.

name: Satu Data Aceh
description: Satu Data Aceh is a provincial government open-data portal for Indonesia running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API, a standardized machine-readable interface over approximately 4,176 datasets, supporting programmatic dataset search, metadata retrieval, and resource access. Because it runs CKAN, it shares a consistent API surface with every other CKAN portal, making it uniformly harvestable and integrable.

description: Satu Data Bencana Indonesia (BNPB) is a government agency open-data portal for Indonesia running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API, a standardized machine-readable interface over approximately 2,830 datasets, supporting programmatic dataset search, metadata retrieval, and resource access. Because it runs CKAN, it shares a consistent API surface with every other CKAN portal, making it uniformly harvestable and integrable.

name: Saudara Ai
description: Saudara AI is an AI-native sourcing brokerage, founded in 2024 and based in Spokane, Washington, that connects American brands with vetted Indonesian manufacturers. Buyers submit requests for quotes (RFQs) and the company pairs human brokers with AI agents that scan factories, verify certifications, benchmark pricing against market data, and prepare quotes, returning vetted supplier options within 48 hours. Saudara AI also handles quality control, logistics, improved payment terms (30/70 and net-60), and vendor financing. As of its launch the company reports having sourced over $1M for 40+ brands. It operates as a brokerage service and does not publish a public developer API, documentation, or SDKs.

name: Shipper
description: Shipper is an Indonesian technology-driven logistics aggregator that connects merchants and e-commerce sellers to hundreds of third-party courier and last-mile delivery partners through a single platform. Its services span a logistics aggregator (multi-courier rate check, order creation, pickup and tracking), nationwide fulfillment and warehousing, contract logistics, international freight forwarding, and e-commerce enablement. Developers integrate via the HTTP-based Shipper Logistics API (v3), which exposes location search, domestic pricing, order creation (including COD), shipping label and receipt generation, pickup request, and shipment status tracking, with real-time delivery-status webhooks. Backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, Partech, and Prosus Ventures.

name: University of Indonesia
description: University of Indonesia (Universitas Indonesia, UI) is a public research university based in Depok and Salemba, Jakarta, ranked #206 in the QS World University Rankings 2025 and the highest-ranked university in Indonesia. Its public, machine-readable developer footprint is limited: UI Scholars Hub, the institutional research repository hosted on the Digital Commons (bepress) platform, exposes a live OAI-PMH 2.0 metadata interface for harvesting scholarly works, and the campus-wide Single Sign-On runs on CAS (Central Authentication Service). No public, self-service developer portal with documented REST endpoints or API keys was found; academic, library, and identity systems are gated behind institutional credentials.
